title: Ainsworth Opens With a Statement
body:
Ainsworth's 165.56 was the week's high score, but the real story is how they got there: Kenneth Walker III (32.6) and D'Andre Swift (31.9) combined for 64.5 points at running back - with David Montgomery (27.4) still sitting on the bench behind them. The resulting 97.06-point demolition of Zogg is the biggest Week 1-2 margin specifically in 13 years of NWL history, shattering the old Week 1-2 mark (Pfaffinger's 68-point win over Conlin, 2015) by 29 points - though it's not the biggest blowout in league history overall; that's still Conlin's 128-point win over Zogg in Week 3, 2019. It is a career-best opening two weeks for Ainsworth personally, who'd never topped 237.8 combined through Week 2 before (2020). Zogg's day was rough top to bottom: nobody on the roster cracked 17 points, including first-round pick CeeDee Lamb (12.9), and the Chargers' Head Coach bonus actively cost them 5 points.

The league's best individual performance belonged to Caleb Williams (37.3) - an 8th-round pick who outscored every quarterback drafted ahead of him and powered Muenchow past Pfaffinger, 133.46-95.3. Glaser's 152.9 (2nd-best team score of the week) rode Derrick Henry (34.8) and Christian Watson (29.7) past Palaia, while 11th-round pick Jalen Coker quietly dropped 29.8 from the bench - a lineup call that didn't end up mattering in a 48-point win. Conlin needed just 129.86 to handle Hagan (78.02), with Josh Allen's 35.7 the league's second-best individual number of the week.

The nightcap was the only real nail-biter: Larson held off Prodahl 101.86-87.92, a 13.94-point margin. Goetz beat Stover 108.06-85.46 behind Jahmyr Gibbs (31.1), the draft's own first overall pick, to round out the slate.

Six games, five double-digit margins, and a Week 1-2 scoring record on the books - Week 1 wasted no time separating the contenders from the rest.

title: Zogg Bounces Back, Three Teams Start 2-0
body:
A week after absorbing the biggest Week 1-2 beating in 13 years of NWL history, Zogg answered with the week's high score - 138.86 - led by CeeDee Lamb (31.3, more than double his Week 1 output) and 11th-round pick Dak Prescott (29.8), to knock off Goetz (75.6) and get back in the win column. The response looks dramatic, but the numbers say otherwise: Zogg's 207.4 combined two-week total is almost exactly their 13-year career average (207.1) for this point in a season - Week 1 was the outlier, not Week 2.

Ainsworth, Glaser, and Larson all won again to open the season 2-0, the only unbeaten teams left in the league - though it means very different things for each of them. Ainsworth's 283.8 and Glaser's 265.9 are both career bests through two weeks, blowing past their previous personal highs (237.8 and 207.4, both set in 2020) by 86-94 points. Larson's 203.5, by contrast, is almost dead-even with their own career average - proof that this league's power rankings (which weight schedule strength, not just raw scoring) have them 3rd rather than 1st for a reason.

Hagan bounced back from a rough Week 1 to beat Pfaffinger 105.06-70.9, even after starting Jalen Hurts (16.2) over a Brock Purdy (28.5, a 13th-round pick) sitting on the bench - a decision that would have flipped a closer game. Pfaffinger's own Bryce Young, picked up as a free agent the same week, delivered 24.1 points in his Pfaffinger debut. Larson handled Palaia 101.68-58.84 - the week's lowest score - behind Patrick Mahomes' 29.0.

The closest game of the week came at the bottom of the standings: Prodahl edged Stover 84.92-72.98, an 11.94-point margin. Through two weeks, Pfaffinger, Palaia, and Stover are all 0-2, and the gap between the top and bottom of the league is already starting to show.
